svg.text: Each version exists because the previous one produced a measured limitation. Red = the problem. Blue = the change. Grey = what was measured.
Nothing is stored. Restart = empty system.
The layers above did not change. That was the
point of the repository interface in v1.
max(1, min(limit, 200)) for non-HTTP callers too
No new library, no new service. The fix was a
bounded interface, enforced at two layers.
WHY EACH VERSION EXISTED — PROBLEM, CHANGE, MEASUREMENT
There is no system yet. A support desk receives free-text
messages and a human reads every one to decide where it goes.
Problem: routing is manual and does not scale with volume.
Requirement: classify the message automatically, and say how sure it is.
FastAPI service, one process, one file.
Model loaded once at startup, not per request.
at concurrency 10, P50 rose to 134 ms — queueing
Everything lived in one file with module-level state. A test
that set app.state.classifier = None broke a different test.
Problem: the code cannot grow, and tests are not isolated.
Also: a classified ticket was returned and then thrown away.
Module per feature, layers inside each module.
create_app() factory — each test gets its own app.
Depends() injects the repository; tests swap in a fake.
Proved: POST on :8000 → id 1, GET on :8001 → total 0
Storage was a Python dict. Restarting the API deleted every
ticket, and two workers each held their own private truth.
Problem: data does not survive, and does not exist once.
Measured, not assumed: ids 1-4 appeared once per worker.
Alembic migration creates the tickets table.
StorageError translated to HTTP 503 at the router.
Only repository.py changed shape. Router and service did not.
GET /tickets returned the whole table. With 13,000 rows one
request occupied a worker for 2.18 seconds.
Problem: the caller decided how much work the server did.
That is an availability risk, not just a slow endpoint.
Enforced twice: FastAPI returns 422 at the edge, and
the service clamps again for callers with no HTTP layer.
list() and count() share _filtered(), so page and total agree.
page query itself: 0.36 ms in the database
Work now depends on limit, not on table size
Every request was anonymous. No column anywhere recorded who
created a row, and anyone reaching the port read every ticket.
Problem: data had no owner, so no rule could be written.
Trigger is a precondition, not a measurement: v5 adds documents.
organizations + users tables; tickets.organization_id NOT NULL.
bcrypt hashing; login returns a signed JWT.
get_current_user runs before every protected handler.
organization_id is a REQUIRED argument: forgetting it is a TypeError,
not a silent leak. Cross-tenant reads answer 404, never 403.
99 tests. Suite 7 s → 103 s, ~60% of it bcrypt.
One caller in a loop could spend the server's CPU: 682 ms of
bcrypt per anonymous login, and /classify was public.
Problem: v3 bounded work per request, not requests per caller.
The same shape as v3, measured in CPU time instead of rows.
Token bucket per caller in core/rate_limit.py, checked by a
dependency BEFORE the expensive work → 429 + Retry-After.
/classify now needs a token. It shares one inference budget
with POST /tickets, so neither is a side door.
A "knowledge" platform with no knowledge: nowhere to store a
document, nothing to read a file, nothing to find a passage.
Problem: retrieval, embeddings and RAG all need stored text.
A precondition, like v4 — turned into numbers by this version.
PostgreSQL tsvector + GIN; keyword search as the BASELINE.
Body-size middleware refuses big uploads before auth.
ts_rank_cd → ts_rank after measuring: 5,909 → 108 ms at 39,588
anon 200 MB: 401 in 4.1 s → 413 in 2 ms
Open after v6 — what the next versions must answer
1. Keyword search misses meaning: paraphrase hit@3 0.47, 20% empty → embeddings + vector search, measured on the same 30 questions.
2. Ingestion blocks the request (300-page PDF 5.8 s, 4.9 MB text 8.4 s) → background processing. 3. Rate-limit buckets are per process.
4. Search cost grows with matching chunks. 5. Originals not kept. 6. No token revocation, no type checker. 7. Suite at 187 s.
